body.statement:
Let \(p_1\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_1)\) and
\(p_2\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_2)\), and suppose a coupling
\((U,V)\) of \(p_1,p_2\) satisfies
\(D=\mathbb E[d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(U,V)]\).  Every
\((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differentially private test has error
\[
 P_e\ge\frac12\max\{1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p_1,p_2),
 0.9e^{-10\varepsilon D}-10D\delta\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(p_1\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_1)\) and \(p_2\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_2)\). Let \((X,Y)\) be a coupling between \(p_1\) and \(p_2\) with \(D=\mathbb E[d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(X,Y)]\). Then for \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(\delta\ge0\), any \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differentially private hypothesis testing algorithm \(\widehat\theta\) must satisfy \(P_e(\widehat\theta,\mathcal P_1,\mathcal P_2)\ge\frac12\max\{1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p_1,p_2),0.9e^{-10\varepsilon D}-10D\delta\}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021), Theorem 1, equation (4), in the PMLR published version.
